It summarizes the key parameters defining the financial, tax, and operational framework, including the proposed lifetime of the plant and the number of years allocated for construction. The table also outlines the guidelines for distributing the total overnight capital cost across the construction period, the effective tax rate, and the depreciation method applied. In addition, it specifies the assumed capital cost escalation during construction and the escalation rate for Operating and Maintenance (O&M) costs during the operational phase. Together, these assumptions provide the standardized basis for estimating plant performance, equipment sizing, and overall cost metrics within the TEA. 3.6.4. Capital cost estimation methodology In general, process simulation using Aspern Plus and Aspen Adsorption and/or spreadsheet calculations were used for the sizing of DAC plant equipment including blowers, vacuum pump, compressor and condensers. Aspen Capital Cost Estimator tool was used to generate a new cost estimate for key process equipment providing both the equipment bare cost and installed cost at a reference year.
